How this is calculated

Nothing above is looked up. It comes from powers of two and a few bitwise steps. Here is the working for the block you typed; it updates as you edit.

    Splitting the block into subnets

    Subnetting is the same powers-of-two idea in reverse. Turn some host bits into network bits and the block divides into equal smaller blocks.

    How many host bits do I need?

    Work backwards from the number of devices. Find the smallest power of two that leaves room for them after the network and broadcast addresses are taken out.

    What is CIDR notation?

    CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) writes an IP network as an address followed by a slash and a number, such as 192.168.1.0/24. The number is the prefix length: how many of the 32 bits in an IPv4 address identify the network. The remaining bits identify individual hosts. The viewer above colours the two groups so you can see exactly where the boundary sits.

    Why subnet sizes are powers of two

    Every host bit can be 0 or 1, so a block with h host bits contains 2h addresses. A /24 has 8 host bits and 28 = 256 addresses; a /26 has 6 and 26 = 64. Moving the boundary one bit to the right halves the block, and one bit to the left doubles it. The step-by-step section above shows the same working for whatever block you enter.

    Frequently asked questions

    What does /24 mean?

    The first 24 bits identify the network and the last 8 identify hosts. That gives 256 addresses, of which 254 are usable because the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address. The netmask is 255.255.255.0.

    How many usable hosts are in a /26?

    A /26 has 6 host bits, so 26 = 64 addresses and 62 usable hosts. The netmask is 255.255.255.192.

    What is the difference between a prefix length and a subnet mask?

    They describe the same thing. A /26 prefix and the mask 255.255.255.192 both say that the first 26 bits are the network. The wildcard mask, used in Cisco ACLs, is the inverse: 0.0.0.63.

    Does this viewer support IPv6?

    The bit view is IPv4 only. The CIDR calculator handles IPv6 prefixes, including how many /64 subnets fit inside a block.

    Can I share a block with a colleague?

    Yes. After you change the block, the page address updates, so you can copy the URL and the other person will see the same block.
